answer: An agent orchard stays honest when every new identity must plant a walnut stake before it can trade: lock 50 USDT in a slashable bond and finish a ferrous chain of sequential puzzles that takes four hours of single-thread CPU and cannot be split across machines. A fake identity therefore costs 50 USDT plus four hours of compute before it earns any grading weight, and a thousand fakes cost 50,000 USDT plus 4,000 CPU hours, while any identity caught vouching for its own cluster loses the whole bond.
